raw_segments.text: I am so glad, she continued, as she sat down opposite to me and took the cat on her knee.
I am so glad you are come.
It will be quite pleasant living here now with a companion.
To be sure it is pleasant at any time, for Thornfield is a fine old hall, rather neglected
of late years perhaps, but still it is a respectable place, yet you know in wintertime one feels
dreary quite alone in the best quarters.
I say alone, Lee is a nice girl to be sure, and John and his wife are very decent people,
but then you see they are only servants, and one can't converse with them on terms of equality.
One must keep them at due distance, for fear of losing one's authority.
I'm sure last winter it was a very severe one if you recollect, and when it did not snow,
it rained and blew, not a creature but the butcher and postman came to the house,
from November till February, and I really got quite melancholy with sitting night after
night alone. I had Lee in to read to me sometimes, but I don't think the poor girl liked the task
much, she felt it confining. In spring and summer one got on better, sunshine and long
days make such a difference, and then, just at the commencement of this autumn,
little Adela Varens came and her nurse. A child makes a house alive all at once,
and now you are here, I shall be quite gay.
